Low-rank bilinear network models

Tosin Salau & Shahryar Minhas

2026-03-25

Source: vignettes/lowrank_dbn.Rmd
lowrank_dbn.Rmd

NOTE: This vignette is under construction. The low-rank model variant is implemented and functional, but the documentation and examples below are preliminary and subject to change.

1 Overview

The low-rank model parameterizes the sender dynamics matrix as At=Udiag(αt)U′A_t = U \, \text{diag}(\alpha_t) \, U', where UU is an orthogonal matrix on the Stiefel manifold and αt\alpha_t is a vector of time-varying factor strengths. This reduces the number of free parameters from m2m^2 to m×r+rm \times r + r, making it scalable to larger networks (50+ nodes).

Use model = "lowrank" when you have many actors and want an interpretable factor decomposition of sender dynamics.

2 Simulate a low-rank network

We start by simulating a 20-node network over 25 time periods with r set to 3. This gives us ground truth to check recovery of the factor structure.

sim = simulate_lowrank_dbn(
  n = 20, p = 1, time = 25,
  r = 3,
  sigma2 = 0.3,
  tau_alpha2 = 0.05,
  tauB2 = 0.03,
  seed = 42
)

dim(sim$Y)
#> [1] 20 20  1 25

3 Memory estimation

Low-rank models store the Stiefel matrix UU and factor paths at each MCMC iteration, so memory usage can grow quickly with network size. Before fitting, you can estimate RAM requirements:

estimate_memory(
  n_row = 20, n_col = 20, p = 1, Tt = 25,
  nscan = 1000, burn = 500, odens = 2,
  family = "ordinal"
)
#> Dynamic DBN memory estimate:
#>   Network:   20 x 20, 1 relation(s), 25 time points
#>   MCMC:      500 draws (nscan=1000, odens=2)
#>   Time thin: 1 (keeping 25 of 25 time points)
#>   --------------------------------
#>   Theta:    0.04 GB
#>   Z:        0.04 GB
#>   A:        0.04 GB
#>   B:        0.04 GB
#>   M:        0.00 GB
#>   --------------------------------
#>   TOTAL:    0.15 GB

4 Fit the low-rank model

The key argument is r, which sets the rank of the factor decomposition. Setting r much smaller than n is what makes this model tractable for larger networks.

fit_lr = dbn(
  sim$Y,
  model   = "lowrank",
  family  = "ordinal",
  r       = 3,
  nscan   = 1000,
  burn    = 500,
  odens   = 2,
  verbose = FALSE
)

5 Model summary

The summary shows posterior means for the variance parameters and the estimated rank structure.

summary(fit_lr)
#> Low-rank Dynamic Bilinear Network model
#>   nodes     : 20 
#>   relations : 1 
#>   time pts  : 25 
#>   rank      : 3 
#> 
#>            mean          2.5%          97.5%        
#> sigma2     54210.442     36011.429     78915.593    
#> tau_alpha2 0.225         0.168         0.294        
#> tau_B2     100000000.000 100000000.000 100000000.000
#> g2         0.146         0.122         0.172

6 Diagnostics

The low-rank plot shows MCMC traces, factor trajectories (αk\alpha_k), and the posterior mean of the node loading matrix UU:

plot(fit_lr)

Scalar parameter traces:

plot_trace(fit_lr)

7 Factor trajectories

The factor trajectories αt\alpha_t capture how each latent dimension’s influence on sender dynamics evolves over time. A flat trajectory means that factor’s contribution is stable; a trending or volatile trajectory suggests structural change along that dimension. Extract factor paths in tidy format for custom plotting:

alpha_df = tidy_dbn_lowrank(fit_lr)
head(alpha_df)
#>   time          mean           lo          hi factor
#> 1    1  0.0053000041 -0.001305681 0.053818449      1
#> 2    2 -0.0088905063 -0.088534301 0.001363029      1
#> 3    3  0.0002627765 -0.001980068 0.002014024      1
#> 4    4  0.0070274876 -0.001512614 0.070152050      1
#> 5    5 -0.0004314414 -0.005152276 0.002132315      1
#> 6    6  0.0186692588 -0.002072614 0.189898130      1
ggplot(alpha_df, aes(x = time, y = mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~factor, scales = "free_y", labeller = label_bquote(alpha[.(factor)])) +
  labs(x = "Time", y = expression(alpha)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "black", color = "black"),
    strip.text.x = element_text(color = "white", hjust = 0)
  )

8 Network summaries

You can compute summary statistics across the posterior distribution of fitted networks. network_summary() returns time-varying means or densities, and edge_prob() gives the posterior probability that each edge exceeds a threshold.

9 Dyad trajectory

Track a specific sender-receiver pair over time with posterior credible intervals.

dyad_path(fit_lr, i = 2, j = 7)

10 Forecasting

predict() propagates the low-rank dynamics forward by H steps, sampling from the posterior to produce forecast distributions.

pred = predict(fit_lr, H = 3, draws = 50, summary = "mean")
dim(pred)
#> [1] 20 20  1  3

11 When to use low-rank

The low-rank model is appropriate when:

  • The network has many actors (50+) making the full dynamic model computationally expensive
  • You want an interpretable factor structure where UU reveals actor groupings and αt\alpha_t captures time-varying factor strengths
  • The rank rr is much smaller than the number of actors

For smaller networks, model = "dynamic" provides more flexible dynamics. For regime-switching behavior, consider model = "hmm".
